The cloud in ice is mostly trapped air
The cloud in ice is mostly trapped air
Tap water holds
dissolved air.
Ice can hold very little.
Your tray freezes
from the outside in,
pushing the air toward
the middle.
The last water to freeze
is packed with air,
so tiny bubbles form
and get locked in.
Freeze it from one side
only,
and the air is pushed
into the last layer.
Cut that off,
and the rest of the ice is clear.
That's why a normal cube
is cloudy in the middle.
